decisions.quote: This paper aims to replicate the full theoretical model of Widener by conducting a survey study to test the LOC framework among Chinese organisations. Most results of our survey study are consistent with those in Widener, which demonstrate the suitability of applying the LOC framework in non‐US settings.
decisions.reason: The abstract distinguishes two levels of conclusion: (1) empirical replication of the 'full theoretical model of Widener' and (2) general theoretical framework suitability ('demonstrate the suitability of applying the LOC framework in non‐US settings'). Under the codebook (Rule 2), demonstrating the general suitability or usefulness of a theoretical framework in a new setting is not an empirical replication verdict on the original study's findings. For the empirical replication of Widener's full theoretical model, the authors explicitly qualify their overall outcome with 'Most results of our survey study are consistent with those in Widener'. Against the stated aim of replicating the full multi-result model, the 'Most' qualifier directly communicates partial empirical replication—that most, but not all, of the model's results were consistent with Widener—which satisfies the codebook definition of 'mixed' ('when some of several tested findings replicated and others did not') without requiring a statistical tally or inferring specific unmentioned failed paths.

scope_review.parent_objection: Does authors overall statement Most results of our survey study are consistent with those in Widener constitute a qualified/partial replication verdict (mixed), or a genuinely affirmative overall verdict (successful)? The first reply treats no explicitly named failed component as excluding mixed. Exact codebook includes partly supporting and partly not, and no statistical tally needed. Do not infer unmentioned specific failed paths; determine what the authors actual most qualifier communicates about full-model replication. Distinguish framework suitability, theory support, and empirical replication outcome. Only abstract supplied; return uncertain if evidence does not settle, with specific reason.

prior_reply.quote: This paper aims to replicate the full theoretical model of Widener by conducting a survey study to test the LOC framework among Chinese organisations. Most results of our survey study are consistent with those in Widener, which demonstrate the suitability of applying the LOC framework in non‐US settings.
prior_reply.reason: The authors state an overall affirmative verdict that their survey results are consistent with Widener (2007) and demonstrate the suitability of the framework in non-US settings. Mentioning that 'most results' are consistent without stating any contrasting or failed finding in the abstract does not establish a mixed outcome.
